title: Hierarchical Access Arbiter with Quota-Fairness for Tiered Traffic
creator: Aditi Rao
description:
Problem: Incoming traffic mixes free, paid, and enterprise tenants. During peak demand we must prioritize enterprise SLAs while preserving fair access for paid and graceful degradation for free tier. Existing simple priority queues lead to starvation or expensive overprovisioning.

Goal: Implement an in-runtime 'Access Arbiter' that enforces hierarchical access (enterprise > paid > free) while using quota-aware prioritization to: (1) prevent enterprise SLA violations, (2) maximize paid revenue throughput, (3) provide predictable degradation for free tier, and (4) minimize overall cost via intelligent fallback to cheaper model variants under pressure.

Acceptance criteria (summary):
- Arbiter enforces per-tenant and per-tier credit pools with soft and hard thresholds.
- Enterprise requests are guaranteed reserved path up to configured reservation; paid has weighted share with short-term deficit borrowing; free gets best-effort degraded models/latency when quota exhausted.
- Fallback mapping to model variants works per-request (e.g., standard->quantized-small->cached-delivery) with clear telemetry indicating fallback reason.
- No enterprise SLO regression in canary (latency P95 within 10% of baseline).
- Cost-per-token for paid tier improves or remains stable under high load due to batching and fallback heuristics.
- Integration tests + chaos run demonstrate no starvation for paid tier over 1 hour of synthetic traffic.

Technical approach (high level):
- Credit accounting: maintain three logical credit pools (enterprise_reserve, paid_pool, free_pool) implemented as leaky-bucket counters in the routing layer. Paid_pool supports weighted deficit round-robin to allow short bursts and limited borrowing from paid_pool to cover transient enterprise overflow under strict caps.
- Admission control flow: request arrives -> route policy checks tenant tier -> consult credit pools -> if allowed, proceed to scheduler; if denied or low credits, consult fallback policy which may: (a) route to cheaper compatible model variant, (b) serve from KV-prefix cache, (c) return 429/soft-fail with suggested retry window.
- Fallback model variants: maintain mapping table per model family. Variants ordered by cost/quality (e.g., f32-large -> quantized-llm -> distilled-faster). Arbiter attaches metadata to request indicating the fallback level used for observability.
- Region interaction: enterprise tenants may be pinned to a region; arbiter must consult region-affinity before reallocating to fallback region. Cross-region fallback allowed only when policy explicitly permits (customer opt-in).
- Telemetry: emit credit_used, credit_remaining, fallback_reason, model_variant, queuing_delay_ms, and per-tenant SLO signals to routing dashboard.
- Runtime performance: credit checks are O(1) metal operations; implement as in-memory atomics with CPU sharding to avoid contention.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict reservation vs overcommit: we choose small enterprise reservations plus limited paid borrowing to reduce idle capacity waste. That risks short transient latency spikes for enterprise if paid borrowing is misconfigured; mitigated with automatic reclamation and conservative defaults.
- Fallback quality regression: routing to cheaper variants improves cost but increases risk of customer-visible regressions. Mitigation: attach 'fallback-score' and enable per-customer opt-out.
- Complexity vs observability: introducing credit pools increases code paths; to compensate, all decisions are logged and surfaced with sampling to reduce telemetry noise.

Deliverables:
- Code: arbiter controller + admission hook + fallback mapping table + telemetry hooks.
- Tests: unit, integration, synthetic load, chaos (node restarts, delayed KV cache).
- Docs: Confluence spec, runbook for tuning credit parameters, public API docs for fallback opt-out.

Links: design brief: https://confluence.redwood.company/SmartRouting/HierarchicalAccessArbiter (internal); initial prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4567 (draft).
acceptance_criteria: Enterprise reserved path enforced and tested in staging (P95 latency within 10% of baseline)
Paid tier maintains weighted throughput without starvation for 60+ minutes of synthetic load
Free tier falls back to designated model variants or cache with clear fallback_reason telemetry
Observability: dashboards for credit pools and per-tenant fallback rates exist and pass review
End-to-end integration test coverage and one canary rollout completed
comments: 2026-03-01 Marcus Chen: Spike completed. Implemented leaky-bucket prototype with atomic counters. Initial microbenchmark shows <0.5us per admission check on 64-core instance.
2026-03-03 Priya Malhotra (PM): Please ensure the paid-borrow window can be toggled per-customer; enterprise customers should be able to opt into 'never borrow' mode.
2026-03-04 Design review (E. Park): Suggested UI knobs for Console: enterprise_reservation, paid_borrow_ratio, free_degrade_threshold. Added to spec.
2026-03-06 Marcus Chen: Added fallback mapping table and basic telemetry tags (fallback_reason, fallback_level). Pushed draft PR 4567. Waiting on infra CI for load tests.

2026-03-08 QA: Found regression in paid fairness when paid_pool weight is high and free_pool exhausted — introduced short-term paid starvation. Proposed change: adjust deficit refill and add 'min-guarantee' for paid tier.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated off by default. 2) Canary with internal enterprise tenants in us-west for 24h. 3) Monitor credit_health and enterprise_p95; if stable, enable for paid customers with opt-in for 48h. 4) Gradually open to free tier with conservative default thresholds. 5) Full release with runtime-1.22 if no regressions.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Misconfiguration can starve paid customers — Mitigation: provide safe defaults and CI validation for weight sums
Risk: Quality regressions from fallback variants — Mitigation: per-tenant opt-out and fallback-score telemetry to trigger rollbacks
Risk: Increased latency due to credit checks under extreme concurrency — Mitigation: CPU sharding and atomic ops, optimize hot paths
notes: Next steps: finalize PR with min-guarantee for paid tier (Marcus), add Console toggle controls (Design + PM), schedule chaos run (SRE).
